bullets.title: AAPL: Jefferies downgrades to Underperform, PT $264 on all-glass iPhone cancellation
bullets.body: Jefferies cuts AAPL to Underperform with PT $263.66 (16% downside) after supply chain checks confirmed cancellation of the 20th anniversary all-glass iPhone due to low production yields. This removes the primary ASP driver, lowering iPhone ASP CAGR FY26-FY31 from 9.0% to 6.8% and cutting FY28/29E EPS by 2.1%/3.4%. Compounding pressure: iPhone 18 Pro memory upgrade appears limited, and JPM notes memory is now 34% of iPhone BOM (up from 10%), with Apple testing Chinese CXMT chips to manage supply squeeze.

bullets.title: INTC: $15B equity offering dilutes CY27 EPS ~3.3%; WFE suppliers benefit
bullets.body: Intel announced a ~$15B common stock offering (plus $2.25B overwriter option) to fund next-gen leading-edge fabs (52/62 AZ, Ireland, then Ohio Fab 27), with aggregate demand exceeding deal size. Dilution estimated at ~6c or -3.3% to CY27 EPS. Mizuho notes INTC has no major customer announcements pre-offering but has >$10B in non-core assets to monetize. Secondary beneficiaries: ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC on incremental WFE demand.

bullets.title: MU: Bullish multi-source consensus — DRAM undersupply to 2028, $250B capex plan, 80%+ GMs sustainable
bullets.body: Micron at KeyBanc forum flagged DRAM supply-demand imbalance persisting beyond 2027 (2027 tighter than 2026), with $250B investment plan and $22B+ in upfront customer cash commitments through 2030. UBS reiterates Buy at $1,625 PT (~11x C2029E EPS of ~$165). Mizuho adds HBM bit growth 50-60% YoY in 2027 still insufficient to meet demand, keeping pricing power intact. Memory sentiment has turned negative (MU -15% since July 1) despite no fundamental change, which Mizuho views as a buying opportunity.

bullets.title: NVDA/SPCX: SpaceX targeting 10GW AI compute by CY27, exclusively on NVDA; $200B+ revenue potential
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag SpaceX building AI infrastructure exclusively on NVIDIA, with Musk targeting ~10GW capacity by CY27 — implying ~$200B in NVDA GPU revenue potential. SemiAnalysis deems 8-10GW feasible; MS notes MSFT could become SPCX's largest compute offtaker at ~3GW, potentially accelerating Azure growth from 42% to >100%. NVIDIA also reportedly investing up to $3B in Lancium (Stargate data center developer).

bullets.title: AVGO: Mizuho sees $225B FY28 AI revenue vs $141-165B Street; 50% TPU share by 2028
bullets.body: Mizuho argues AVGO is positioned for 18M+ TPU units by 2028E with ~50% share (~10-12M units, 3x current volume) in Google TPU training chips. FY26 AI revenues estimated at $72B, FY27 consensus $141-165B, vs Mizuho's $225B FY28 estimate. Bear thesis that AVGO loses Google share to MediaTek seen as unsustainable; Hock Tan expected to take offensive stance on the September 2 earnings call.

bullets.title: AMD: Taalas acquisition tackles memory wall; Wolfe sees 163% DC revenue growth CY27
bullets.body: UBS highlights AMD's acquisition of Taalas as addressing the memory wall via a differentiated approach while expanding custom silicon offerings. Wolfe's Chips with Caso webcast projects AMD 70% YoY server CPU growth and 163% YoY data center revenue growth in CY27, with a base $20 EPS and $25 bull case. Notebook ODM weakness (PC shipments -27% MoM in July) represents a headwind for AMD's consumer segment.

bullets.title: CSCO: Q4 earnings preview — beat likely but FY27 guidance could disappoint at 25x NTM
bullets.body: UBS rates Buy at $132 PT; expects Networking revenue ~$9.6B (+26% YoY), product orders +35% last quarter (strongest in decade), and Oct FY1 guidance $16.6-16.8B. However JPM flags risk that FY27 guidance disappoints given stock is up ~60% YTD and trades at 25x NTM — consensus expects $16.82B Q4 revenue and $1.17 EPS, with options implying ~8% move. CSCO has beaten EPS in 20 of the last 20 quarters.

bullets.title: MSFT: Custom Maia 300 chip targets Sept 2026 unveiling; SpaceX partnership a potential Azure inflection
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports MSFT is escalating custom AI silicon with Maia 300 targeting a September 2026 unveiling with 300K+ chips in 2027 (vs. tens of thousands of Maia 200s). MSFT potentially becoming SpaceX's largest compute offtaker at ~3GW, which MS says could accelerate Azure growth from 42% to >100% next year. The Information confirms Maia chips now deployed in Azure data centers after overcoming initial delays.

bullets.title: HPE: Morgan Stanley upgrades to Overweight on FOMP-driven enterprise hardware cycle
bullets.body: MS upgraded HPE (and P/Everpure) to Overweight, shifting IT Hardware sector from Cautious to In-Line, citing 'Fear of Missing Procurement' pull-forward in enterprise spending — 70-75% of CIOs pulling forward 2026 Server/Storage/PC spending. AlphaWise survey confirms cycle driven by refresh and AI. HPE was up ~5% in pre-market. MS sees Server/Storage upcycle extending to 2027-2028; prefers Storage > Servers > PCs.

bullets.title: NET: Cloudflare re-accelerating but launches $2.175B convertible; FedRAMP High adds TAM
bullets.body: Hedgeye is bullish on NET post-earnings: revenue +36% YoY (re-accelerated 4 of last 5 quarters), large customer adds +27% YoY, DBNR +120%, RPO +38%, gross margin up 30bps for first time in 8 quarters. Headcount cut ~14% while guiding higher revenue signals productivity inflection. Cloudflare also achieved FedRAMP High Authorization (plus GovRAMP Moderate), opening federal/DoD markets. Stock down 2.1% in pre-market on the $2.175B convertible offering.

bullets.title: APP: Hedgeye short thesis — model improvement slowing, Q3 guide disappoints
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains active short on AppLovin: Q2 NRPU growth slowed to +58% vs +93% in Q1, install volume -2%, and EBITDA flow-through declining sequentially. Q3 guide implies only +7.6% sequential growth vs prior low-to-mid teens, suggesting the latest model release is insufficient to sustain the prior pace. Hedgeye attributes the slowdown to loss of first-party games data (post-divestiture) and ML diminishing returns.

bullets.title: HUBS: Hedgeye short — FY26 revenue guide cut $22M, customer adds halved, AI costs rising
bullets.body: HubSpot beat reported P&L but Hedgeye flags deteriorating fundamentals: FY26 revenue guide cut $22M, expected net new customer adds halved to 5,000-6,000, and subscription COGS +37% YoY vs revenue +18% as AI inference costs pressure margins. NRR flat for the year; CEO acknowledged April was slow and the expected quarter 'did not materialize.' Non-GAAP margin beat was driven by buybacks and tax rate cuts, not operational improvement. Stock -1.4% pre-market.

bullets.title: TTD: DA Davidson downgrades to Neutral, PT $16; significant share losses, multi-quarter recovery
bullets.body: DA Davidson cut The Trade Desk to Neutral with a $16 PT after TTD missed materially on Q3 revenues and EBITDA, with guidance drastically below consensus. Management cited macro headwinds at large global clients and lacks visibility on spend churn. Davidson expects a sizeable restructuring in coming months and a multi-quarter recovery. DSP seen as a share gainer given mid-market domestic advertiser mix. TTD was down 2.2% in pre-market.

bullets.title: UBER: Jefferies elevates to Franchise Pick, $110 PT on 20% bookings growth and AV scaling
bullets.body: Jefferies elevated UBER to Franchise Pick with a $110 PT, citing durable ~20% bookings growth and growing confidence in scaling autonomous vehicles. LYFT also reported a solid Q2 (gross bookings $5.50B beat $5.37E; EBITDA $177M beat $172E) but KeyBanc maintains Sector Weight, noting Q3 guidance of $5.50-5.67B is slightly below Street at $5.58B.

bullets.title: DKNG: 2Q miss significant but prediction markets driving 75% YoY customer acquisition; Citi raises PT to $32
bullets.body: DraftKings reported 2Q Adjusted EBITDA of $115M, missing Street significantly (-62% YoY vs. Street -45%), with revenue of $1.44B below guidance. However, customer acquisition rose 75% YoY and the Predictions product attracted 600K+ customers YTD. Citi raised PT from $30 to $32, cutting FY26/27 EBITDA but raising FY28 estimate. Hedgeye separately flagged iGaming showing no real improvement despite marketing spend.

bullets.title: META: Recommits to open models; Muse Glimmer 30B released; $1B data center community fund
bullets.body: META CEO Zuckerberg publicly recommitted to open-weight models, releasing Muse Glimmer 30B (runs on single consumer GPU) and establishing a $1B fund to invest in local communities hosting AI data centers. Stock +1.7% in pre-market. Morgan Stanley notes META as a key AI adopter beneficiary; MS CIO Wilson prefers hyperscalers including META over semis in current cycle.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi maintains Buy; Week 32 CCU data implies Q3 bookings $1.68B above guidance high-end
bullets.body: Citi's RoMonitor shows Week 32 average peak CCUs of 16.2M, up 3% sequentially (though -21% YoY). Using a conservative $51 bookings/payer assumption, Citi projects Q3 bookings of $1.68B, above the company's $1.57-1.65B guidance range and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.61B. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: Semis PC headwind: July notebook ODMs -27% MoM; KeyBanc cuts Q3 forecast to -4% QoQ
bullets.body: KeyBanc's July notebook ODM analysis shows shipments of 12.2M units vs. 13.3M estimate, down 27% MoM and 19% YoY. Quanta missed 26% (weak Apple demand), Compal missed on weak Dell demand. Q3 forecast cut to 41.9M units (-4% QoQ, -12% YoY); full-year 2026 forecast -8% to -12% YoY. PC-exposed names AMD, INTC, MU, and NVDA face incremental headwinds from this data point.

bullets.title: FSLY: KeyBanc forum highlights 20%+ revenue growth, 117% NRR, 70% compute growth — execution turnaround intact
bullets.body: Fastly at the KeyBanc Technology Leadership Forum: 20%+ YoY revenue growth, NRR at 117% (4-year high), compute revenue +70% YoY, and record gross margins exceeding long-term targets. RPO (commit-based contracts) up 38% YoY improves visibility. Leadership overhaul since mid-2024 credited for improvement. No GPU/AI infrastructure investment planned; focus remains on CPU-based edge compute.

bullets.title: BABA: GS previews Q2 with cloud expected +45% YoY; tactically constructive on China soft-tech ADRs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs expects BABA cloud revenue to accelerate 7 points to 45% YoY when it reports August 20, with GS anticipating an EPS revision cycle bottom. GS strategists turned incrementally more constructive on offshore internet ADRs vs hard-tech peers, citing substantial underperformance, trough valuations, narrowing subsidy losses, and improving AI monetization. China internet profits forecast to decline -12% YoY in the June quarter — a significant improvement from -35% and -31% in Dec/Mar quarters.
